//: EXAMPLE — the external-CLI registry read by sk-cli-executor / sk-cli-orchestrator.
//1: DO NOT hand-edit the live file. Manage it only with the CLI verbs (Rule 1 — .sidekicks/ is the
//2: CLI write surface): `sidekicks cli-executor register|list|remove`. This example documents the shape.
//3: Live file is scope-resolved: root -> .sidekicks/cli-executors.json ; project -> projects/<active>/cli-executors.json.
//4: A MISSING file is not an error — the three built-ins apply by default (fresh-clone behavior unchanged).

claude.//: kind=generic — Claude Code's own CLI registered as an executor (claude -p headless). Commonly the MAIN/default pick: put it first in routing.prefer so `executor: auto` items resolve to a fresh headless Claude, with the other CLIs picked by specialty/availability.
claude.//permissions: claude -p runs under Claude's own permission system, NOT an external sandbox. For tasks that must EDIT files headlessly you may add a permission mode to the invoke template (e.g. add '--permission-mode' + 'acceptEdits'). A permission-BYPASS flag is deliberately NOT set here (safety — never auto-approve beyond the documented headless setting).
claude.//models-top: `top` = the tier ABOVE high (Fable/Mythos-class; CLAUDE.md → 'Fable fallback'). Map it only where the CLI truly offers one — set with `register <name> --model-top <id>`; executors without one leave it unmapped and the orchestrator routes top-shaped work to an executor that maps it, or requests high explicitly.
claude.//model_specialties: OPTIONAL per-tier job pairing — for each configured model tier, the jobs THAT model is best at, so the orchestrator picks an item's model_tier by fit ('right job on the right model'), not just generic complexity. Set with `register <name> --model-specialties-high 'a,b' --model-specialties-mid '...' --model-specialties-low '...'` (empty value clears a tier). Advisory metadata — drives no flag.

codex.//: kind=builtin only toggles a native adapter (codex/gemini/antigravity). Omit to keep the default; set enabled:false to silence it.

models.//: OPTIONAL per-complexity model map. The orchestrator picks a tier by task difficulty; the executor resolves tier->id here and passes the CLI's model flag (codex -m, gemini -m, agy --model). Set with `register codex --model-high <id> --model-mid <id> --model-low <id>`.
models.//1: IDs are machine/account-specific — these are ILLUSTRATIVE, not real. An absent map or unmapped tier means no flag -> the CLI's own default (pre-feature behavior).

codex.//specialties: OPTIONAL capability hints the orchestrator routes tasks against (via `list --json`) — short phrases, no closed vocabulary, drive no flag. Set with `register codex --specialties 'a,b,c'`.

my-cli.//: kind=generic is a NEW CLI driven entirely by this spec via adapter_generic.py — no bespoke adapter.
my-cli.//invoke: Arg template. Placeholders: {brief}=brief text, {brief_file}=path to brief on disk, {work_dir}=abs workspace, {model}=resolved model id. Must contain {brief} or {brief_file}, OR set brief_stdin:true.
my-cli.//model: Keep the model flag+value in ONE token (`--model={model}`): when no model resolves, the whole token is dropped, leaving no orphaned flag. A CLI with no model flag simply omits {model}.
my-cli.//probe: Optional side-effect-free reachability/auth check; exit 0 == available. Omit to treat 'binary on PATH' as available. Never runs a task turn.
my-cli.//sandbox: Informational containment label recorded on the result: kernel-sandbox | vm-isolation | cli-sandbox | constraint-block-only | unknown.

routing.//: OPTIONAL auto-routing policy. `prefer` is an ordered fallback chain — `--executor auto`
routing.//1: (or an orchestrator item executor:auto) probes these in order and takes the first AVAILABLE.
routing.//2: Manage with `sidekicks cli-executor route set claude codex` / `route` / `route clear`.
routing.//3: Unset → auto falls back to every enabled executor in natural order (built-ins first).
routing.//4: prefer[0] is the MAIN pick for `executor: auto` — put claude first to make it the default, others the fallback.
routing.//skills: OPTIONAL per-task-kind RECOMMENDATIONS — 'for THIS kind of job these executors work best, in order' — consulted BEFORE the global prefer chain when the task kind is known. `prefer` is the ordered best-fit chain; `avoid` names executors that must NOT take this kind of job; `note` says why. Manage with `sidekicks cli-executor route skill set <task-kind> <name>... [--avoid '<a,b>'] [--note '<why>']` / `route skill remove <task-kind>` / `route skill`.

image-generation.note: Claude CLI has no native image generation — route visual/image jobs to Gemini-backed Antigravity first, Codex second
